summary: Tairyo Makita was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Bukkyo University (~1929–1933) and Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1957–1976) and later as president of Saitama Institute of Technology (~1995–2002).
Tairyū Tsunoda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a lecturer post at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and became a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Taisei Iwata is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 1996).

Taishu Tagami is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1958) and earned a master's at the University of Tokyo (~1963–1965). He served as professor at Komazawa University (~1984–2005) and taught at the Eastern Institute (attested 1990).
Taishun Mibu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his studies at Taisho University in 1937. He later served as director at Taisho University (attested 1972).

Taitetsu Unno was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1947–1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1951–1968). He served as a professor at Smith College from ~1971 to 1999.

Taixu was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jichan (~1904–1907). He founded several institutions, including the Minnan Buddhist Institute (1918), which he led in 1927, the Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1922), and the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1930–1931).
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies. Sze completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen.
Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2015, he was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1945–1953). He served Ryukoku University as professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (1970) and president (1989–1995), and chaired the Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (attested 2013).

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1900–1902), Waseda University (~1902–1905), and the University of Paris (~1916–1920). He held an academic post at Waseda University from ~1906 to 1940.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who was a doctoral candidate at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2003). Inoue served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Taisho University and Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Heinz Bechert. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1999).
Takanobu Takahashi was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Shitennoji University (~1989–1996) and the University of Tokyo (~1996–2016), where he served as an associate professor.

Takanori Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Komazawa University (~1966–1970). He worked as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1979) and lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996).

Takao Hayashi is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1968–1974) and Brown University (~1980–1985) under David Pingree. He served as Professor of History of Science at Doshisha University (~1986–2019).
Takao Kagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held faculty posts at Rissho University (~1967–1975; attested 1981), Mejiro University (attested 1988), and Shinshu University (~1980–1994), where he became professor emeritus.

Takao Moriyasu was a Central Asian and Iranian history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977) and Osaka University. He held positions at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Kanazawa University, and as professor at Osaka University (~1992–2012).

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1952–1961). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1965–2003) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).
